newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt decision postponed, minstry says.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt decision postponed, minstry says.

text.p: The Austrian government on Thursday said it would not make a statement on a last-ditch offer for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein by a group around insurer EA-Generali before the start of next week.

Finance Minister Viktor Klima earlier this month indicated he would reveal his final decision about the bid by the consortium, which includes Germany's Commerzbank and Banca Commerciale Italiana, by the end of this week.
"It really wouldn't make sense to rush it. The minister is going to Dublin on Friday, and the decision will be made post-Dublin," a spokesman for Klima told Reuters.
Klima is scheduled to attend a meeting of European Union finance ministers in Dublin over the weekend.
EA-Generali earlier on Thursday said it expected to hear Klima's final word on the offer by Friday.
"I would assume that he will indeed make a statement on Friday," a spokesman for the Austro-Italian insurer said.

Klima over the past two weeks has repeatedly hinted the group's bid, submitted on September 6 just hours before a government deadline expired, failed to meet his demands for an all-cash offer for the government's entire 70 percent voting stake in Austria's flagship bank.

EA-Generali reportedly has offered cash for about half the government's 19.9 million Creditanstalt shares and proposed to sell the rest in a secondary offering, possibly financed via a convertible bond issue.

Klima has threatened to reopen the already six-year long privatisation process to other potential bidders if he and his advisor, London investment bank J.P. Morgan, decided the group's proposal is insufficient.
There have been no reports of any other potential buyers, even though Klima indicated he had received calls by several interested parties.

A number of international candidates, among them Allianz Holding of Germany and CS Holding of Switzerland, over the past few years have lost interest in Creditanstalt after what they felt was a bias against foreign ownership in Austria.
Allianz just last week denied resurfacing rumours that it was still interested in Creditanstalt, which has a strong presence on the emerging markets of central and eastern Europe.
EA-Generali and Creditanstalt already have close links with each other, and the bank sells the entire range of EA-Generali's insurance products over its counters.
EA-Generali chief executive Dieter Karner sits on Creditanstalt's supervisory board, while Creditanstalt chief Guido Schmidt-Chiari, is a member of EA-Generali's non-executive board.

The consortium was thrown into disarray just hours before Klima's deadline expired when Die Erste, Austria's biggest savings bank, left the group after hectic negotiations with its partners failed to produce agreement on a joint bid.
Die Erste last week left its options open in what has become Austria's longest-running privatisation drama, saying it was waiting for Klima's final word and would then re-evaluate its position.
